title: Rebreather-style closed helium loop for etch and ALD chucks
idea: Adapted from closed-circuit diving rebreathers, which scrub and recirculate expensive heliox instead of venting it. Each tool gets a foreline tap that captures backside-cooling helium leaking past the e-chuck (plus leak-check station exhaust), strips it through a getter cartridge and cold trap, and recompresses it into the chuck supply loop.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline since March 2026). Fabs vent almost all backside He; 85-95% per-tool recapture cuts purchased helium ~5-10x and buffers spot shortages.

title: Turbo-generator hydrogen cooling replaces helium on wafer chucks
idea: Adapted from large power-plant turbo-generators, which are cooled with pressurized hydrogen because its thermal conductivity beats helium's. Feed electrolyzer-made H2 at ~5-15 Torr into the sealed e-chuck backside gap of deposition, implant and non-H-sensitive etch tools, with generator-style purity monitors, dilution exhaust below LEL and purge interlocks.
why: Removes the largest fab helium use (backside cooling). H2 conductivity ~0.18 W/mK vs He ~0.15, and it is made on site from water and power, so the supply is domestic and unlimited.

title: Optical-fiber soot deposition makes synthetic-silica crucible inner walls
idea: Adapted from outside vapor deposition (OVD) used to make optical-fiber preforms. SiCl4-derived silica soot is deposited on a rotating crucible-shaped mandrel and sintered into a 3-5 mm fully synthetic inner layer. That layer is backed with ordinary lower-grade fused silica, so no Spruce Pine HPQ ever touches the melt.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity quartz chokepoint. SiCl4 is a cheap polysilicon by-product, and a synthetic liner lowers metal contamination and may lengthen crucible life.

title: Cold-crucible levitation melting adapted from aerospace titanium skull melting
idea: Aerospace titanium is melted in water-cooled segmented copper cold crucibles, where induction fields push the melt off the wall and a thin frozen skull is the only contact. Adapt this to Czochralski growth: hold the silicon melt in an induction cold crucible with a solid-silicon skull and pull the crystal from the free surface.
why: Eliminates quartz crucibles entirely (Spruce Pine) and the oxygen they dissolve into the crystal, cutting per-ingot consumables. The challenge is getting a calm enough melt for dislocation-free growth.

title: Solar kerfless epitaxial wafers grown on reusable porous-silicon seeds
idea: Adapted from the solar industry's kerfless wafer process: epitaxial silicon is grown from trichlorosilane on a porous-silicon release layer atop a reusable template, then detached. Grow 150-300 um, 300 mm DRAM substrate wafers directly from gas and reuse each template 20-50 times.
why: Skips Czochralski pulling, quartz crucibles, argon-hungry pullers and wire sawing. Substrate energy roughly halves, and crucible plus polysilicon intensity per wafer falls >3x.

title: Gemstone-style cleaving recovers backside slabs from thinned memory wafers
idea: Stacked and HBM DRAM dies are ground from 775 um down to ~30-50 um, so >90% of the crystal becomes sludge. Adapt gemstone cleaving: after the front side is bonded to a carrier, an IR laser writes a buried damage plane ~60 um deep, and a thermal-stress pulse splits off a ~650 um slab that is repolished into a new wafer.
why: Each pulled wafer yields a second wafer, roughly halving crystal, quartz-crucible and energy per HBM bit. It also eliminates grinding sludge and grinding water.

title: Catalytic-converter-style smelting recovers tungsten from fab chamber waste
idea: Adapted from autocatalyst PGM recycling, which combines a collection network, assay-based pricing and smelt-and-refine. Collect W-coated chamber shields, spent W sputter targets and WF6 abatement scrubber sludge, oxidize them, refine via ammonium paratungstate and refluorinate to WF6 domestically.
why: Tungsten is ~80% Chinese, and CVD W uses only a small fraction of the delivered WF6; the rest ends up in abatement. Recovering 30-50% of fab tungsten flows creates a domestic secondary supply.

title: Copper-mine by-product molybdenum replaces tungsten in buried wordlines
idea: Adapted from copper miners' practice of recovering molybdenite as a by-product (Utah and Arizona porphyries). Contract US mine molybdenum into MoCl5/MoO2Cl2 ALD precursors and switch buried-wordline and bitline-contact fill from TiN/W to barrier-thin Mo.
why: Removes the China-80% tungsten chokepoint from the cell array using a US by-product metal. Mo's lower resistivity at narrow widths also cuts wordline RC ~15-25%.

title: Space-station water recovery chain for 95% ultrapure-water reclaim
idea: Adapted from the ISS water recovery system: vapor-compression distillation, multifiltration beds, catalytic aqueous-phase oxidation and conductivity-gated reject loops. Segregate rinse streams by contamination class at every wet bench and run each class through a modular distillation and catalytic-oxidation skid that returns water to UPW polishing.
why: Fabs draw ~10+ ML/day of water and typically reclaim 40-70%. A 95% closed loop cuts intake ~5x and makes fabs viable in arid US sites (AZ, TX, NM).

title: Dry-cleaner supercritical CO2 replaces water rinses after etch
idea: Adapted from dry cleaning's switch from perchloroethylene to supercritical CO2. Strip post-etch polymer residue and dry high-aspect structures in scCO2 with small co-solvent doses, with the CO2 recycled through a separator and compressor; with no surface tension, tall pillars cannot collapse.
why: Cuts UPW and IPA in the many post-etch cleans (~20-30% of fab water) and removes the yield loss from capacitor-pillar leaning at 60-75:1 aspect ratios.

title: Soybean transformer oil replaces fluorinated fluids in fab chillers
idea: Adapted from utility transformers, which moved to natural-ester fluids (soy-based, high flash point, biodegradable), and from avionics polyalphaolefin coolants. Use stabilized ester/PAO blends as the heat-transfer fluid in etch-chuck and tool chillers instead of perfluoropolyether (Galden) and hydrofluoroether (Novec) fluids.
why: 3M has exited PFAS fluid production and PFPEs face the EU PFAS restriction. Ester/PAO fluids remove a single-source PFAS dependency for all chillers above about -20 C.

title: Pharmaceutical cyclic-olefin polymers replace fluoropolymer wetted parts
idea: Pharma prefilled syringes use cyclic olefin polymer (COP/COC) because it has extremely low leachables. Adapt COP-lined, PEEK-bodied valves, filters and distribution lines for UPW and non-oxidizing dilute acids in place of PFA/PVDF, keeping fluoropolymer only for ozone, peroxide and solvent service.
why: Fluoropolymer piping is a PFAS regulatory risk and a concentrated supply. UPW loops are the largest wetted surface in a fab, so converting them roughly halves fluoropolymer mass.

title: Pulp-mill chlorine-free bleaching chemistry replaces sulfuric-peroxide wafer cleans
idea: Paper mills replaced chlorine bleaching with totally chlorine-free ozone/peroxide sequences. Adapt that sequence: replace SPM (piranha) resist strips and SC-1 cleans with ozonated DI water carrying dissolved CO2, followed by UV-activated peroxide, all generated on site from oxygen, water and electricity.
why: Fabs buy thousands of tonnes a year of 96% sulfuric acid and peroxide. Ozone chemistry cuts purchased chemical mass ~80%, along with trucking and neutralization load.

title: Caterpillar-style remanufacturing harvests DRAM from retired servers
idea: Adapted from Caterpillar Reman's core-deposit model. Hyperscalers return DIMMs from 4-6-year-old servers for a credit; a reman line desolders DRAM packages, burns them in, screens them at derated timings and rebuilds them into modules for edge, PC and CXL-pooled capacity tiers.
why: Retired servers hold enormous DRAM volume. Recovering even 30% adds supply with zero new wafers, helium, quartz or tungsten, at perhaps 30-50% of new cost per bit.

title: LNG terminal cold energy runs fab nitrogen and chillers
idea: Adapted from Japanese LNG import terminals, which use regasification cold (-162 C) to power air separation and cold storage. Site a fab beside a US regas terminal (e.g. Cove Point, Elba Island, Everett) and drive its nitrogen air-separation unit and process chillers from LNG cold through an intermediate loop.
why: Nitrogen generation and chillers are a large share of a fab's energy load. LNG cold cuts ASU electricity ~50% and chiller power ~30%.

title: Nuclear-reject unseparated zirconium-hafnium feeds capacitor dielectrics
idea: Nuclear-grade zirconium is expensive mainly because neutron-absorbing hafnium must be stripped out, but DRAM ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 dielectrics tolerate and can even benefit from Hf. Make Zr ALD precursors directly from unseparated zircon (natural ~2% Hf) and use the Hf as a tetragonal-phase stabilizer.
why: Skips the energy- and solvent-intensive Zr/Hf separation run by very few plants worldwide. Precursor cost falls maybe 30-50%, and separated Hf is freed for logic HKMG.

title: Phosphate-fertilizer fluorosilicic acid becomes domestic electronic-grade HF
idea: Florida phosphate plants scrub fluorosilicic acid (H2SiF6) out as a waste stream. Adapt the fertilizer industry's FSA-to-fluoride routes to crack FSA into anhydrous HF, then distill it to ppt-grade for wafer etch and for NF3/WF6 synthesis.
why: HF depends on fluorspar (China ~60%). US phosphate by-product fluorine could cover domestic fab HF demand, removing a mining chokepoint.

title: Steel-mill air separation units retrofitted to capture neon
idea: Ukraine's semiconductor neon came from crude-neon columns on Soviet steel-mill air separation units. Adapt this by bolting crude neon/helium columns onto US integrated-steel and chemical-plant ASUs and purifying the output into excimer laser gas for the DUV ArF/KrF layers that still pattern most of DRAM.
why: Neon historically came ~50% from Ukraine/Russia. Capture at ~20 existing US ASUs could cover domestic fab demand without new air-separation capex.

title: PCB-etchant electrolytic regeneration recycles persulfate cleaning chemistry on site
idea: PCB shops electrolytically regenerate spent cupric-chloride etchant instead of buying new. Adapt this to wafer cleaning: electrolyze spent sulfuric cleaning streams on boron-doped-diamond anodes to regenerate peroxydisulfuric acid as the oxidant in a closed loop at each wet bench.
why: Cuts sulfuric acid and H2O2 purchases ~70-90%, along with their trucking and waste. The diamond electrodes can be made domestically.

title: Glass-cullet recycling turns spent fab quartzware into crucible feedstock
idea: Adapted from glassmakers' cullet remelting. Collect retired diffusion tubes, wafer boats, etch rings and bell jars (all made from HPQ fused silica), plasma-melt them, strip surface metals with chlorine-gas refining, and refuse the result into crucible inner-layer sand.
why: Recovers HPQ that was already mined at Spruce Pine. Fabs scrap tonnes of quartzware each year, so this cuts new HPQ demand ~10-20%.

title: Cultured quartz from oscillator industry crushed into crucible sand
idea: The quartz-oscillator industry grows ultra-pure cultured quartz in hydrothermal autoclaves, using low-grade quartz as nutrient. Run large autoclaves purely for crucible feedstock, then crush and acid-leach the cultured bars into <10 ppm-impurity HPQ sand.
why: Turns abundant low-grade quartz into Spruce Pine-equivalent purity, ending dependence on a single deposit. The risk is autoclave throughput and cost.

title: Ugly-produce partial-good DRAM dies with fused-out banks
idea: Adapted from grocers selling cosmetically imperfect produce. Bin DRAM dies that have dead banks or subarrays, which are normally scrapped, as partial-good parts: on-die fuses remap the address space, an SPD field reports usable capacity, and OS/CXL memory managers consume the odd-sized capacities.
why: Recovers ~3-8% of wafer output at advanced nodes. Each recovered bit already carries its full embedded helium, quartz, tungsten and energy, so it comes at zero extra resource.

title: MLCC core-shell titanate grains for an abundant high-k capacitor
idea: Multilayer ceramic capacitor makers flatten BaTiO3 permittivity with core-shell grains (a ferroelectric core inside a doped paraelectric shell). Adapt this as an ALD nanolaminate of SrTiO3 cores with Ba/Mg-doped shells on a TiO2-templated TiN electrode to reach k ~70-100 in a 6 nm film.
why: Fact 1 says k ~70 is needed. Titanates use abundant Ba/Sr/Ti instead of Hf/Zr and let pillar aspect ratio fall from ~70:1 toward ~40:1, cutting deep-etch fluorocarbon gas and helium-cooled etch time.

title: HVDC thyristor valves shrunk into a capacitor-free bulk-silicon latch
idea: Grid HVDC valves hold state as latched pnpn thyristors that stay on at minimal holding current. Adapt a vertical pnpn thyristor per bit in plain bulk silicon, gated by the wordline to latch or unlatch, with a sub-uA hold current only on active rows and a slow-decay off state elsewhere.
why: Deletes the whole capacitor module: Zr/Hf ALD dielectric, TiN electrodes, nitride support lattice, and the 60:1 fluorocarbon etch with its helium-cooled chucks. That is ~20-30% fewer process steps and ~35% less PFC gas per wafer.

title: Architectural low-E glass zinc-tin-oxide for an indium-free gain cell
idea: Low-emissivity window coaters sputter zinc stannate (ZTO) over huge areas of glass every year. Adapt their target chemistry and rotary-sputter tooling to a two-transistor, zero-capacitor gain cell whose wide-bandgap ZTO write transistor leaks sub-fA, so the read transistor's gate holds the bit for seconds.
why: Removes the capacitor plus indium and gallium (heavily China-concentrated) from oxide gain cells. Zn and Sn have diversified supply, and the BEOL process stays below 400 C.

title: Dry-lubricant molybdenite monolayers as a domestic-supply gain-cell channel
idea: Molybdenite (MoS2) is mined in Colorado mainly for lubricants and steel. Adapt CVD monolayer MoS2 (1.8 eV gap, no dangling bonds) as the write transistor of a capacitor-free gain cell, where the 2D channel's tiny off-current lets the read transistor's own gate hold charge for seconds or longer.
why: Capacitor-free and indium-free, built on a US-mined element. Retention could cut refresh energy >100x (Fact 3).

title: Rare-earth-free motor magnet chemistry for platinum-free MRAM
idea: EV-motor makers are replacing NdFeB with iron nitride (Fe16N2) and synthetic tetrataenite (L10-FeNi). Adapt these phases as the perpendicular free and reference layers of a spin-torque cell, removing Pt/Co multilayers, the Ir in the synthetic antiferromagnet and heavy Ta seeds.
why: MRAM is capacitor-free with very high endurance but leans on Pt, Ir, Ru and Ta (South Africa/Russia/DRC chokepoints). Iron and nitrogen are everywhere.

title: Planar ferrite inductors revive core memory at micron scale
idea: Power-supply makers now print MnZn/NiZn ferrite planar cores on silicon. Adapt this to bring back magnetic core memory: a 1-2 um ferrite toroid per bit, threaded by BEOL wordline, bitline and sense traces, with coincident-current writes and on-die restore-after-read.
why: Core was DRAM-class working memory before DRAM: no capacitor, no leakage, no refresh, unlimited endurance, all iron/manganese/zinc oxides. Density is the hurdle; the aim is ~10-20 F2 per tier across many stacked BEOL tiers.

title: RF filter aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric in an endurance-shielded cell
idea: Phone BAW filters are sputtered aluminum nitride made in vast volume. Adapt boron-doped AlN (a ferroelectric wurtzite needing no Sc or Hf) as a ferroelectric-gated transistor bit on the same sputter tools, and shield its finite endurance with an SRAM write-back buffer that absorbs hot writes so each cell sees <1e9 cycles over its life.
why: A capacitor-free, Hf-free, Sc-free nonvolatile bit needs no refresh. The risks are the high coercive field (~4-6 MV/cm) and fatigue.

title: Keyboard snap-dome physics as a contactless bistable nanobeam bit
idea: Keyboard snap-domes and pressure-relief discs use buckled shells with two stable states. Adapt this as a pre-stressed silicon-nitride nanobeam per bit that snaps up or down under electrostatic pulses and is read without contact through piezoresistive strain or a MOS gate underneath.
why: No capacitor, no leakage path and no refresh, using only Si and SiN (no Hf, W or In). A contactless snap avoids stiction, so endurance could exceed 1e15, and GHz-scale nanobeams switch in ~1-10 ns.

title: Parametron revival using MEMS-timing resonators storing phase bits
idea: MEMS timing chips (silicon resonators that replaced quartz crystals) meet Goto's 1950s parametron. Each bit is stored as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped nanomechanical resonator; one shared pump tone holds every bit, and reads use phase-sensitive detection.
why: No capacitor and no leakage tail, in all-silicon. Refresh is replaced by a continuous low-power pump, possibly ~fW per bit for high-Q resonators. Density and speed are unproven.

title: Microwave tunnel-diode latch makes a refresh-free one-transistor SRAM
idea: Microwave oscillators exploited the negative resistance of Esaki tunnel diodes. Adapt two series Si/SiGe interband tunnel diodes as the bistable load on a single access transistor (1T-2TD), forming a static latch at roughly 2x DRAM-cell area with no capacitor.
why: Eliminates both capacitor and refresh (Fact 3) using only Si, SiGe and dopants. It needs a room-temperature peak-to-valley ratio >3 at very low valley current.

title: Thermochromic-window vanadium dioxide as a Mott-transition latch cell
idea: Smart-window coatings switch VO2 between insulator and metal. Adapt a strain-tuned nanoscale VO2 element in series with an access transistor, using the transition's hysteresis window to hold two stable resistance states, with vanadium recovered from US steel slag and refinery residues.
why: A capacitor-free cell with a sub-ns transition, using vanadium from domestic waste streams instead of China/Russia. It trades refresh for a small hold bias.

title: Solar-cell silicon nitride charge layers become a dynamic trap bit
idea: PERC solar cells rely on stable fixed charge stored in silicon nitride passivation. Write that charge on purpose: a 1T cell with a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide under a SiN trap layer, programmed by direct tunneling (not Fowler-Nordheim) for 10-100 ns writes, retention of seconds to minutes, and low-field cycling.
why: No capacitor, no Zr/Hf high-k and no deep etch, only Si/SiO2/SiN. Refresh is ~1000x rarer than DRAM's; trap-cycling endurance is the open risk.

title: RF SiGe quantum wells hold holes in a floating-body cell
idea: Adapt the bandgap-engineered SiGe base of RF heterojunction transistors by burying a thin SiGe quantum well below a vertical-channel transistor. Holes generated by band-to-band tunneling collect in the well and shift the threshold, and the valence-band offset stretches retention far beyond plain floating-body cells.
why: A capacitor-free bit in bulk silicon plus a few % germanium, avoiding the capacitor etch and dielectric. The germanium can come from US zinc-smelter residues.

title: Solar-grade silicon plus RAID coding tolerates leaky capacitorless cells
idea: Solar uses cheaper upgraded-metallurgical silicon, and RAID tolerates failing disks. Combine both: build capacitor-free floating-body or gain-cell arrays on 6N-7N wafers and absorb the fatter leakage tail with row-level erasure codes that rebuild expired bits instead of refreshing everything faster.
why: Siemens polysilicon purification (~50-60 kWh/kg) and 11N purity are energy and supply chokepoints. Tolerating impurity-driven tails could cut substrate energy and cost ~20-30%.

title: Southwest Airlines single-fleet logic for a minimal-tool capacitorless fab
idea: Southwest flies a single aircraft type to slash spares, training and maintenance. Adapt this by designing a capacitor-free cell flow (no pillar etch, no ZAZ ALD, no support lattice) that runs on ~6 standardized shallow etch, deposition and litho tool families, sharing spares, chamber kits and gases fab-wide.
why: Dropping the capacitor removes the most helium- and fluorocarbon-intensive tools. Fewer tool types cut capex ~25% and halve spares inventory and specialty-gas SKUs.

title: Organic-food certification model for PFAS-free capacitor-free memory
idea: Copy USDA Organic's audited-label model. Certify memory made in flows free of perfluorinated etch gases, PFAS photoacid generators and fluoropolymer wetted parts, which becomes achievable because a capacitor-free cell drops the 60:1 fluorocarbon etch, and sell it at a premium to EU buyers facing PFAS restrictions.
why: Turns the EU PFAS squeeze into market pull for a resource-light flow. PFC emissions per wafer fall ~50%+.

title: CD-stamping nanoimprint patterns capacitorless arrays without EUV
idea: Optical-disc plants stamped nanoscale pits from nickel masters by the billion. Adapt jet-and-flash nanoimprint with replica templates for the repetitive array layers of a capacitor-free vertical-transistor cell, where there is no landing-pad-to-capacitor overlay chain to break, and keep DUV only for periphery.
why: EUV has one supplier, draws ~1 MW per scanner and consumes tin and hydrogen. Imprint uses ~1/10 the energy and no EUV, and removing the capacitor removes the hardest overlay stack.

title: LCD panel fabs build capacitor-free memory on Gen-8 glass
idea: Display fabs pattern oxide TFTs on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass at a tiny fraction of wafer cost per area. Adapt idle Gen-6/8 oxide lines to make capacitor-free gain-cell memory sheets that are diced into tiles and bonded as a capacity tier behind CXL controllers.
why: No Czochralski crystal, quartz crucible, EUV or helium-intensive deep etch. It suits bulk far-memory capacity where density per area matters less than cost per area; density at ~0.5-1 um rules is the main limit.

title: ACSR power-line composite conductors replace tungsten array lines
idea: Overhead power lines pair conductive aluminum with a strong steel core. Adapt this for a capacitor-free BEOL array: wordlines and bitlines are Al cores with a 1-2 nm Mo or TiN skin that blocks electromigration and diffusion, which works because capacitor-free BEOL cells never exceed ~400 C.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and the tantalum barrier from array lines. Aluminum is abundant and smelted in the US, and low-temperature capacitor-free flows make it viable again.

title: PCB direct metallization replaces tungsten plugs in shallow cells
idea: PCB makers coat through-holes with a graphite colloid and then electroplate copper directly. Adapt this with a conformal CVD amorphous-carbon seed plus electroplated Co or Cu fill for cell contacts, made feasible because a capacitor-free cell has only shallow ~5:1 contacts instead of deep storage-node plugs.
why: Eliminates WF6 CVD (tungsten plus fluorine) for contacts and uses aqueous plating with abundant chemistry.

title: Antifouling-paint copper oxide and varistor zinc oxide form oxide SRAM
idea: Marine antifouling paint consumes Cu2O by the kiloton, and surge arresters use ZnO. Adapt p-type Cu2O and n-type ZnO thin-film transistors into a complementary BEOL latch: a static 4T/6T cell stacked in multiple tiers over logic.
why: Refresh-free bits with no capacitor and no indium, from abundant Cu and Zn oxides; multi-tier stacking recovers density. The risks are Cu2O hole mobility and off-current.

title: Vertical-farming stacks memory tiers on logic, deleting separate wafers
idea: Vertical farms grow many crop tiers on one footprint. Adapt this by depositing 8-16 tiers of capacitor-free BEOL memory directly over the accelerator's logic die, replacing HBM's separate DRAM dies, base die and TSV stack.
why: HBM consumes ~3x the wafer area per bit plus 8-12 separate CZ wafers per stack. Monolithic tiers use no extra crystal or quartz crucible per bit and remove the TSV tax (Fact 6) and much of the data-movement energy (Fact 5).

title: Coca-Cola bottler franchise for a portable capacitorless memory module
idea: Coca-Cola ships concentrate and lets local bottlers add abundant local water. Adapt this by licensing a capacitor-free BEOL memory concentrate (PDK, recipes, precursor specs, test IP) that any CMOS fab, including US 28-65 nm and MEMS fabs, bottles onto its own wafers with local, non-chokepoint materials.
why: Spreads memory supply across dozens of existing fabs with no new $15B fab. It uses only BEOL-temperature steps that are light on Hf, W and He, and could lift the US share well above 2%.

title: Zero-waste garment cutting reclaims wafer-edge area with tiny tiles
idea: Zero-waste fashion nests pattern pieces to use the whole bolt of cloth. Lay out capacitor-free memory as 1-2 mm2 self-contained tiles (own sense amps, redundancy and BIST) that fill the partial-die ring at the wafer edge, then sell them as chiplets binned by tile count.
why: Large DRAM dies waste ~6-10% of each wafer at the edge. Tiny capacitor-free tiles avoid the capacitor-height non-uniformity there and recover most of it, cutting crystal, quartz and energy per bit proportionally.
